cells.tense: You are looking at what is actually in front of you, and you are steady while you do it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing today you have been sorting with old reasons, and say your reason for it out loud in one plain sentence.
cells.core:
You're seeing what is actually there right now. Not the version you expected, not the one you were braced for — the plain thing in front of you. And from that you're saying this, not that, which is why it feels clean. Not forced. The difference between one thing and another is visible to you right now, and you're using it.

That first clear look is worth keeping. It doesn't need defending yet. It arrives, it shows you, and then you point. What you point at today will grow legs. There's a reason for it, and the reason is yours — say it in one plain sentence before you act on it.
cells.sheetLine: You can see what is here and point at it without forcing.

cells.tense: You are deciding ahead of what is actually here, and the decision keeps arriving before the moment does.
cells.ask: Leave one plan unwritten for a day, and be where you are when the next thing actually arrives.
cells.core:
You're jumping to the decision before the moment has shown you anything. A glance comes in and you've already named it, filed it, picked the direction. You get no full second of looking at it. That speed buys you certainty you don't have yet, and it costs you what you actually want: to see what is there before you close it.

There's nothing wrong with wanting it clear in. But what you're deciding at that pace is a rehearsed call. Stay one beat longer. Let the thing sit unnamed until it has shown you its shape. What you're reaching for is already here, waiting for the second you stop deciding and start looking.
cells.sheetLine: You decide before you look, and the open moment goes missing.

cells.tense: You stood at the moment when a direction could have been chosen, and you did not choose it, and you are still standing there.
cells.ask: Write down the one thing you keep not deciding, and write next to it the reason you are holding off.
cells.core:
There's a direction you left alone. You saw the moment — and some part of you is still at that hinge, waiting for it to come around again. It hasn't. Meanwhile you watch yourself not pick, from a slight distance, and the day moves on without the call.

The clear look isn't what's gone. You can still tell one thing from another. What went quiet is the pointing. Start with the smallest possible one, today. One thing you will set a direction on, and follow for an hour. Let the act itself remind you what it feels like to point and mean it.

cells.tense: You are already choosing what this is and what it is not, and you talk as if the choosing were done by someone else.
cells.ask: Catch one moment today when you point at something and say what it is, and say out loud that the pointing is yours.
cells.core:
You point at things all day and say what they are. That phone call is a chore. That plan is off. Somebody is making those calls, and it's you — and you describe it like the day made them, or the situation did, or the facts did. You're steering without saying so.

That's a strange thing to hold, because it means the room you're in is partly your shape. Not in a big way. In the way a room looks different once you say what's in it. Try catching one of those moments today. Say what it is. Then say that you were the one who said it. Nothing heroic — just the plain acknowledgment of what you already did.
